lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: Listen. Then act it out consolidates the unit language within a narrative context. Students listen to understand the story's plot and character motivations, then role-play the dialogue to practise fluency and intonation.
Look for attentive listening, understanding of the plot twist (the surprise), and confident delivery of the dialogue with appropriate emotion and intonation.
“Do you like surprises? I do! Do you want to read about a special surprise for Minh? Let's listen to her conversation to find out what the surprise is!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.29 - B. Choose the correct answers.

details: Choose the correct answers checks students' comprehension of the story. The questions require them to recall specific details and understand the underlying reasons for the characters' actions.
Look for accurate selection of the answers for all three questions, demonstrating a clear understanding of the story's plot and character motivations.
“That was a fun story with a nice surprise! I’m not sure I understood everything though. Can you help me choose the correct answers? Let’s go!.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.83 - A Read, write, and number.

details: Read, write, and number consolidates narrative comprehension skills. Students must use context clues to complete the dialogue with the correct words and then number the story frames in the correct logical sequence.
Look for accurately completed sentences using the word bank and correct numbering of the story frames from 1 to 6.

“Oh no, I don’ t understand this story at all!  It’s all mixed up! Some of the words are missing, and the pictures are in the wrong order. Can you be a story detective, write the missing words, and number the pictures to fix it?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - C Make your own story.

details: Make Your Own Story encourages creative language use and personalization. Students complete the story template with their own ideas, then act out their unique version to practise speaking fluency.
Look for creatively and logically completed sentences in the story, and confident, enthusiastic role-playing of the new dialogue with a partner.
“I want to write a new surprise story! Will you help me? Think of your own ideas for places and presents, fill in the blanks to create your story, and then perform it for your friends.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.30 - Tongue Twisters Listen & say

details: Listen and say provides focused pronunciation practice on the consonant blends 'st' and 'sm'. The tongue twister format encourages students to articulate the sounds clearly and at speed.
Look for clear and accurate articulation of the 'st' and 'sm' consonant blends, even when students attempt to say the sentences quickly.
“Now for a fun challenge! Let's try to say some tricky tongue twisters. Listen carefully to the 'st' and 'sm' sounds, then see how fast you can say them without getting your tongue in a twist!”
